Case Reason 1 of 12
Payroll Reversal
Correcting a payroll after wages and tax debits have already been initiated. This action cannot be undone — always ask the right questions before proceeding.
Cancel vs. Reverse — What's the Difference?
CancelReverse
When to useBefore debits are initiated (before 4pm CT / NACHA not yet created)After debits have been initiated
What happensCanceled payrolls are not deleted from Panda — they move to the Unfunded section of Employee Payrolls, where they can be fully deleted if necessary (e.g. system bug resolutions). The admin can still make edits and reprocess from there.Original stays on backend; new "reversed" payroll created; can target all OR select employees
Who can do itAdmin can cancel in-app — always encourage self-serve first. Agents can also cancel in Panda. Note: there is a brief window where canceling is unavailable in-app due to cutoff times, but remains available in Panda. Check the Actions drop-down to confirm which options are live.Gustie in Panda, or admin in-app (as of 2023)
💡
If an admin can cancel their own payroll, always encourage them to take that action on their account first.
Before Reversing — Ask These 4 Questions

⏰ WHEN are we reversing?

Before check date: Fine to pull funds.
After check date, <5 business days: Can still pull funds.
>5 business days after check date: Cannot legally pull funds (but can still reverse the payroll).

👤 WHO are we reversing?

Confirm employee names. Can reverse the entire payroll OR just select employees. You must reverse the entire paycheck — not just the overpaid portion.

📋 WHAT are we reversing?

Net Pay & Taxes: Full reversal — pulls back wages and tax reporting entirely.
Just Net Pay: Convert to check — changes payment method from DD to check.

📊 Guideline 401(k)?

Before check date: Reverse without looping in Guideline.
After check date: Written approval from Guideline is required before processing the reversal — email clients@guideline.com. Note: approval is not always guaranteed (e.g. Guideline may decline for FIT withholding elections).
Two Types of Reversals

Full Payroll Reversal

Pulls back wages + taxes entirely. Use when a mistake was made — wrong amount paid, wrong employee, wrong quarter. Must reverse the entire paycheck (can't reverse just part of it).

Convert to Check

Changes payment method from direct deposit to check. Use after a bank error is received by Gusto — never in anticipation of a bank error. Wages are still reported; just the payment delivery changes.
⚠️
Bank error rule: Never reverse a payroll because a bank error is anticipated. Let the bank error play out — Gusto receives the error code in 2–3 business days and the system handles it. Acting prematurely creates unnecessary delays.
Running a Reversal in Panda (7 Steps)
  • 1
    Go to "Most Recent Payrolls" and select the check date you are reversing
  • 2
    Click Actions dropdown → Select "Reverse Payroll"
  • 3
    Select "Reverse Entire Payroll" OR select specific employees
  • 4
    Choose whether to select "Pull Employee Funds" (requires admin's written consent; NACHA takes 5 business days). Exception: if it is after the debit date but before the check date, pool funds must be selected — explicit admin approval is not required in this window as no other option is available.
  • 5
    Leave notes — include the case number and reason for reversal
  • 6
    Click "Create Payroll Reversal"
  • 7
    Approve the reversal — must be done the same day!
Tax & Wage Implications
⚠️
Never promise the customer that: (1) wages will never be deposited into the employee's account, or (2) Gusto can guarantee recovery of funds already paid. We only have one attempt to pull funds — if that fails due to a bank error, the company must work with the employee directly.
Tax StatusWhat it meansWhat happens
PendingTax has NOT been sent to the agency yetReversing will refund the tax amount in a few business days. Verify deposit schedule — liability status is delayed by a day.
PaidTax HAS been sent to the agencyReversing will NOT refund. Company waits until end of quarter (or year for FUTA) when agency sees overpayment.
Reversals in closed quarters automatically flag for amended returns. If in a prior year, the system generates a W-2c within 24–48 hours.
Reversing Contractor Payments (4 Steps)
  • 1
    Open the check date → Actions menu → "Reverse Contractor Payment"
  • 2
    Enter a reason and click "Create Contractor Payment Reversal." Before check date: payroll funds must be selected (same as a payroll reversal). After check date: Gusto is not authorized to reverse funds from a contractor — do not attempt to pull funds.
  • 3
    No additional approval needed — but thoroughly check all details before clicking "Process Contractor Payment Reversal"
  • 4
    Leave a comment with your case number, WHY the reversal occurred, and WHO was reversed

Case Reason 2 of 12
Auto Wage Correction (AWC)
A system-generated correction tool that recalculates taxes for a specific time period based on updated information — without requiring manual entry.
What is it?
An Auto Wage Correction (AWC) is a payroll correction tool Gusties run in Panda to recalculate taxes after something changes — like a backdated address, a tax exemption update, or a risk class code correction. The system does the math; you review and submit.
⚠️
Before running any AWC: Always screenshot the current tax summary first. This lets you predict the outcome and catch unexpected changes before they happen.
When do you use it?

🏠 Backdated Address Change

An employee's home or work address was updated retroactively, changing which local/state taxes apply.

🛡️ Tax Exemption Changes

A company or employee-level tax exemption was added or removed for a past period.

🏗️ Risk Class Code Correction

A WA or WY workers' comp risk class code was wrong and needs to be corrected for past payrolls.
The 3-Step Process
  • 1
    Prepare Take a screenshot of the tax summary. Check the debit/agent payment summary to predict whether the correction will result in a debit or refund. Set clear expectations with the customer before running.
    • Confirm all settings in Panda are correct first (RCC, exemptions, address, rates)
    • Determine if the correction falls in a current or closed quarter
    • Check the company's Join Date to confirm Gusto can file for those quarters
  • 2
    Run the AWC In Panda → Employee Payrolls → Actions → "Run Auto Wage Correction Payroll."
    • Select the beginning and end dates (must be within the same quarter)
    • Current quarter: use the last actual check date in the quarter
    • Monthly filers: use the last day of the month, not the last day of the quarter
    • Do not check "Pay Employee State & Federal Withholding taxes" — employees reconcile on their own tax return
    • Click "Preview Wage Correction"
  • 3
    Review & Submit The preview shows original vs. corrected amounts, subject wages, gross subject wages, and impacted taxes.
    • Review carefully — incorrect taxes can sometimes appear, or a tax may be missing
    • Leave a detailed comment with your case number
    • Click "Run Wage Correction" only when the preview looks correct
Tax Implications

✅ Underpaid Taxes

The company owes more than was collected. A debit will happen the day after the AWC runs. Check the payroll debit date.

💰 Overpaid Taxes

More was collected than owed. Whether Gusto can refund depends on whether the quarter is open or closed and whether taxes have already been remitted to the agency.
Quarter StatusTaxes NOT yet paidTaxes ALREADY paid
Current QuarterSet taxes to pending in Panda — refund in 3–5 business daysGusto will request refund amounts in the original return at end of quarter
Closed QuarterFile a Payments JIRA (manual NACHA) if AWC didn't auto-trigger a refundCustomer must wait for amended return process — agencies send refund to company (not employee); typically takes 6 weeks (Pufferfish)
🚫
Gusto can only debit/remit taxes if: the company was with Gusto during that quarter AND Gusto submitted original filings. Check the company's Join Date. If filings show as "Rejected," corrections cannot be re-filed.
Key Terms
Subject Wages
Wages subject to a specific tax; YTD should never exceed the wage base limit.
Gross Subject Wages
Total taxable wages for this tax — reflects benefits/imputed income; will not reflect wage base limits.
Gross Wages
Total wages earned — usually matches the paystub salary.
SW vs. GSW
The AWC preview shows both Subject Wages (SW) and Gross Subject Wages (GSW) — both should shift after a correction.
Pufferfish
Gusto's internal tax filing system. Speaks directly to Panda. Covers IRS, CA, OH WH, NY, IL.

Case Reason 3 of 12
Exempt Taxes
Managing tax exemptions at the company or employee level — and knowing when to use the CFIP (Company Filing Inactivity Period) Blocker tool instead.
What is it?
A tax exemption removes the obligation to collect or remit a specific tax for a company or employee. Exemptions may apply to federal, state, or local taxes and are usually granted based on legal status (e.g., nonprofit, religious org, realtor). Gusto supports two levels: company-wide exemptions and employee-level exemptions.
🚫
We cannot advise on whether a company qualifies for a tax exemption. Always direct the customer to their CPA or tax advisor. Our role is to implement what they tell us.
Company-Wide vs. Employee-Level Exemptions
TypeWhat it doesWho handles itExamples
Company-WideApplies the exemption to all employees at the company levelAdmin self-serves in Gusto app (Taxes & Compliance → Tax Setup)Nonprofit SUI exemption, religious org exemptions
Employee-LevelApplies the exemption to one specific employeeAdmin self-serves on employee's profile (Pay tab)Employee FICA exemptions, student FICA, minister housing
Setting Customer Expectations
  • Direct customers to their CPA or tax advisor to confirm eligibility before making any changes
  • Company-wide exemptions are self-served by the admin — walk them through where to find it
  • Employee-level exemptions are also self-served — direct them to the employee's Pay tab
  • After an exemption is added or removed, an AWC must be run to correct past payrolls
  • Exemption changes in past quarters require an AWC first, then a tax recon
Common Examples

📌 MA Unemployment Exemption

Some nonprofits or religious orgs are exempt from MA SUI. Admin configures at the company level. After adding, run an AWC to back-correct.

📌 TX Unemployment — Realtors

Real estate agents who are independent contractors may be exempt from TX SUI. Confirm with the customer's attorney before applying.

📌 WA FMLI CFIP Blocker

When a company improperly uses a company-wide exemption to stop $0 filings — use the CFIP Blocker tool instead.
Blocking $0 Tax Filings — The CFIP Blocker Tool
⚠️
Common mistake: Admins sometimes add a company-wide exemption just to stop $0 filings. This is incorrect — it can affect all employees and cause compliance issues.
The correct solution is the Internal CFIP Blocker Tool. Here's how it works:
  • 1
    Identify the problem — Company has been using a tax exemption just to prevent $0 filings, not because they are genuinely exempt.
  • 2
    Remove the incorrect exemption — Work with the admin to remove the improperly applied exemption.
  • 3
    Apply the CFIP Blocker (CFIP = Company Filing Inactivity Period) — Use the Internal Filing Blocker Tool (IKB: Tax Process: Blocking $0 Filings). This blocks the specific filing, creates a $0 draft, and auto-restarts if the employer re-hires.
ℹ️
The CFIP Blocker automatically creates $0 draft filings so nothing falls through the cracks. If the employer rehires employees, the blocker reactivates automatically.

Case Reason 4 of 12
Non-Gusto Payroll (Externals)
Entering payroll data that was processed outside of Gusto — ensuring quarterly and annual filings, W-2s, and tax amounts are accurate.
What is it & Why does it matter?
A Non-Gusto Payroll (also called an External) is any payment that was processed outside of Gusto, or was not entered historically during onboarding. Entering these in Gusto ensures that:
  • Quarterly and annual forms accurately reflect subject wages and tax amounts (including W-2s)
  • Amendments necessary for prior quarters are triggered correctly
💡
Default approach: Non-Gusto payrolls should almost always be entered by the customer in-app. Only Tier 2 processes externals in Panda when self-serve is not possible.
Non-Gusto Payroll vs. Off-Cycle Payroll

There are two ways to account for payrolls not processed in Gusto — choosing the right one matters for tax accuracy.

Non-Gusto PayrollOff-Cycle Payroll
Who enters itCustomer self-serves in-app (or Tier 2 in Panda)Customer self-serves in-app
WagesPaid outside of GustoPaid/reported through Gusto
QuarterUsed for closed quarters in most cases. Use for the current quarter if some or all taxes were already remitted by the company (e.g. prior provider wages)Used to report wages in the current quarter only
TaxesAdmin specifies which taxes are prepaid vs. pendingAll associated taxes are debited by Gusto
Real-World Examples

Example 1 — Off-Cycle ✅

Email 5/1/24 · First check date 4/3/24

Admin paid an employee $1,500 on April 10th but forgot to run it through payroll. No taxes were paid.

Why off-cycle? The check date falls within the current quarter. Instruct admin to run an off-cycle payroll.

Example 2 — Non-Gusto ✅

Email 3/17/24 · First check date 2/15/24

Admin had a payroll in early February processed by Paychex. Some taxes were already paid by the prior provider.

Why Non-Gusto? Payroll was processed outside of Gusto. Instruct admin to enter a Non-Gusto payroll in-app.

Example 3 — Non-Gusto ✅

Email 4/18/24 · First check date 3/31/24

Admin discovered Q1 previous payroll wages were overstated by $500 for an employee — entered during onboarding.

Why Non-Gusto? Processed outside of Gusto prior to joining. Reverse the original historical payroll in Panda, then re-enter as Non-Gusto specifying which taxes were prepaid.
When to Say NO to an External Request
⚠️
There are a few instances where we do not fulfill a request for an External:

📅 Amendment Policy

We can amend accepted returns that Gusto originally filed, for up to 3 full tax years after the original filing period.

🏢 Historical Payrolls with a PEO

All payrolls from the customer's time with a PEO will be included on quarterly/annual filings and W-2s under the PEO — not Gusto.

⚠️ Intentional Misuse of Platform

Intentionally not submitting payroll throughout the year to avoid paying taxes. You can warn the customer we will not accommodate these corrections in the future, but perform them as a one-time courtesy. Be sure to add a comment in the company's Panda so we don't continue granting one-time courtesies.
Before Processing — Information Needed from Admin

💰 Wage, Tax & Benefit Amounts

  • Regular hours, gross earnings, additional earnings
  • Benefit deductions
  • Admin should provide tax amounts. If they did not withhold tax, they can use Gusto's tax calculations.

🏦 Tax Payments

Mark as Prepaid: Admin already remitted tax payments outside of Gusto.

Mark as Pending: Gusto needs to debit/remit taxes on behalf of the company. Only available if Gusto filed for taxes within that quarter.

Important: We must debit SUI in the current quarter. For quarters the customer was not with us, the only tax we can debit is FUTA.
Can We Debit?
ScenarioCan Gusto Debit?
Current Quarter✅ Gusto can debit & remit any taxes
Closed QuartersOnly if Gusto originally filed for that quarter. Review Quarterly Form Filings in Panda to confirm which quarters/agencies Gusto successfully filed for.
FUTAWe can debit for FUTA as long as the external is for the current year
Pufferfish AgenciesTaxOps will support original filings/payments for all Pufferfish agencies triggered after the deadline, up until their last re-file attempt date (1 month after quarter closes)
Benefit Implications — Check for GMB First
🚫
Before reaching out to the admin, check if the company has active Gusto-Managed Benefits (GMB). If they do, route the case to Tier 2 — Benefits.
  • 1
    From the company's main Panda page, check for the Benefits pill at the top of the screen. If present, confirm the benefits are active (expired benefits = NOT a GMB case).
  • 2
    Click Hippo in the top right corner of the Panda page (no Hippo button = no GMB).
  • 3
    In Hippo, scroll to the Current Benefits / Active Subscriptions screen to confirm whether GMB is active.
  • 4
    If active GMB is confirmed → route the case to Benefits Tier 2.
In-App vs. In Panda — Which Do We Use?
Whenever possible, instruct the admin to enter the Non-Gusto payroll in-app. This way, they learn to self-serve and there is less work for advocates. However, if you have all the information needed, you can enter it yourself in Panda for a better customer experience — then send them the steps so they can self-serve in the future.
⚠️
Common situations where we will enter the payroll manually in Panda:
  • The correction is required due to a Gusto error or the admin is escalated
  • The system is not allowing the admin to enter the payroll in-app due to a bug
  • FEIN Change scenario — customer already ran payroll on the new FEIN account (see FEIN Change training)
Entering the External Manually in Panda (9 Steps)
💡
Quick callouts before you start:
  • Drafts: You can navigate away and the draft will be saved. If you cancel before processing, it stays in draft form.
  • Garnishments/Reimbursements: Not necessary to include — both are post-tax with no tax implications. Reimbursements can be added in-app by the admin. Garnishments can be added via MWC or as an EE deduction for a Custom post-tax benefit in rare cases.
  • Different Tax Liabilities: Taxes can only be debited in full. If only a portion was paid, mark that tax as prepaid and have the admin remit the remaining portion directly to the agency.
  • Washington & Oregon work hours: Must include number of hours worked due to state filing requirements. Optional for all other states.
  • 1
    In Panda, go to External Employee Payrolls on the company's main page, then click the red "Navigate to external payroll tool" button in the top right corner.
  • 2
    Confirm the admin cannot enter in-app. Scroll down and click "Add a non-Gusto payroll." Select the reason for entering (Payroll Migration, Minister Housing, Stock options, Additional wages for net pay, Customer refuses, Employee retention credits, or Other).
  • 3
    Enter your Salesforce case number, pay period (optional but recommended), check date, a detailed comment (Ticket Info — required), and debit date (optional, defaults to next business day).
  • 4
    Select the impacted employees from the dropdown menu.
  • 5
    Enter wage and tax amounts. Use "Edit Columns" to deselect unneeded columns and rearrange order. Click "Prefill EE/ER tax amounts" to use Gusto's tax calculations. Note: only active states with assigned addresses are available for state tax — if an employee was paid in a different state with their previous provider but has since moved, the previous address must be added first.
  • 6
    Compare with Gusto's tax calculations and fix any errors. Discrepancies are highlighted in yellow — click the highlighted row to find the cell with the error. For unexpected amounts, check EE hire dates, exemptions, etc. Tax rates used will reflect current Gusto settings at the time of entry.
  • 7
    Select which tax liabilities should be marked as prepaid (already remitted by admin) and mark taxes that should be debited as pending. You can mark all liabilities at once using the dropdown. Enter any accrued credits if applicable. Click "Create Payroll."
  • 8
    Click "Preview unprocessed payroll in Panda" to review before fully submitting. Once everything looks correct, click "Process payroll and initiate debits."
  • 9
    Review the final payroll in Panda. Confirm debit and refund amounts & dates with the admin, both at a company and employee level. The comment you added will automatically appear at the top of the fully submitted Panda page.
💡
Pay stubs: Externals do NOT generate pay stubs in the employee's profile. If needed, admins can retrieve them by navigating to the "Employee Hours and Earnings" drop-down within payroll history.
Tax Reconciliation — Don't Skip This Step!
⚠️
After entering a Non-Gusto payroll, run auto-recons for each impacted quarter — and each following quarter up to the most current check date.

Why Run Recons?

Recons ensure the tax summary is trued up and that corrections will not cause downstream errors or failed filings.

What to Look For

  • Reallocation of wage bases (FUTA, SUI, etc.) to the first earned wages of the year
  • Any rounding discrepancies
  • Big changes in amounts withheld due to inaccurate tax rates
  • Anything unexpected that needs further research
Checking Amendments
Changes to wages and taxes for previous quarters require amended filings. Key rules:
  • Amendments are automatically generated
  • Gusto can only generate an amendment if we successfully filed the original filing for the company
  • Double-check that we both generated the filings and they were successful in the Quarterly Form Filings section of Panda
  • You can view the amendment in Pufferfish to confirm the filing date — amendments on quarterly filings take 4–6 weeks to process, longer during end of year
Checking W-2Cs
💡
W-2Cs are now generated automatically through Pufferfish. If Gusto did not generate an original W-2 for an employee, we cannot generate an amended W-2.
  • 1
    Head to Pufferfish and click Update Filters to find the company's W-2C
  • 2
    Use the company's ID and other information to find the filing, then click the Filing ID to navigate to Filing details
  • 3
    Click Regenerate Filing Data to refresh and see changes made in Panda
  • 4
    Click Preview and confirm the changes are reflecting on the W-2C
  • 5
    Note: W-2Cs can take up to 48 hours to show in-app

Case Reason 6 of 12
Tax Reconciliation Payroll (Recon)
Running tax recons to collect or refund money after key events — keeping taxes current and preventing downstream errors like failed filings and agency notices.
What is a tax recon?
A tax reconciliation payroll ("recon") looks at total subject wages and associated tax rates, then calculates what taxes should be. If collected taxes are above or below that corrected amount, Gusto debits or credits the company's bank account. There are two types: automatic quarterly recons and Gustie-triggered recons after key events.
🚨
Recons are VERY important. Skipping or delaying a recon after a key event causes downstream errors — agency notices, failed filings, and delayed corrections. Always run one promptly, even if the corrections look unfamiliar.
What do recons correct?

✅ Recons DO correct:

  • Social Security (both portions)
  • Medicare & Additional Medicare (both)
  • FUTA (employer) & FUTA adjustments
  • State Unemployment & surcharges (ER)
  • SUI for NJ and PA (employee)
  • PFL for NJ, CT, DC, MA, WA (EE)
  • NM Workers Comp, VT Health Tax, WY Workers Comp
  • NY MCTMT, NV MBT
  • Local: Denver OPT, MA EMAC, OR Eugene CSPT, Jersey City Tax, Newark City Tax

❌ Recons do NOT correct:

  • Federal Withholding Tax (employee)
  • State Withholding Tax (employee)
  • AK State Unemployment (employee)
  • Everything else not listed (check the Reconciliation Payrolls IKB)
What events require a recon?

Run a recon directly after:

  • SUI rate changes
  • Adding or removing external payrolls
  • Benefit adjustments
  • Auto or manual wage corrections
  • Payroll reversals (closed quarters only)

Run AWC first, then recon:

  • Risk class code changes
  • Owner's Draw → Salaried/Hourly changes
  • Exemption changes (added or removed)
  • Courtesy withholding changes
  • Employee address changes
Running a Recon in Panda

Navigate to the company page in Panda → Operations → "Recons"

  • 1
    Select the debit date, year, and quarter
  • 2
    The draft recon runs first — review the preview before submitting
  • 3
    Check results: summary now shows breakdown by "Monthly" and "Quarterly" taxes, and separates "Taxes due to employee payroll" from "Taxes not attributable to individual employees"
  • 4
    Leave a comment explaining why the recon is being run (include case number)
  • 5
    Submit — customer emails are sent for any recon debit > $5
ℹ️
Bulk Recons: For running recons on multiple companies at once, use Taxes → "Bulk Recons" in Panda. Enter comma-separated company IDs or upload a file. Useful for batch corrections after a widespread rate change.

Case Reason 7 of 12
Workers' Comp — WA & WY
Understanding Washington and Wyoming state workers' compensation — how premiums work, how to troubleshoot failed filings, process Risk Class Code corrections, and handle tax implications.
The Basics
Washington and Wyoming require employers to get coverage through a state fund. Gusto will deduct insurance premiums on behalf of the employee and employer and remit to the state along with a filing at the end of each quarter.

🏛️ Washington Workers' Compensation

Premium rates are based on associated Risk Class Codes (RCC) and rates assigned to the business by the agency.

💡
Risk Class Codes are different from Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes. SOC codes are also required for Washington employees — see Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes for more information.

🏔️ Wyoming Workers' Compensation

Premium rates are based on your business classification under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS).

💡
The Wyoming Workers' Compensation rate that should be entered in Gusto is listed on the notice as the experience rate, not the base rate.
Troubleshooting Failed Filings
Failed filings typically have one of three root causes:
Root CauseWhat it Means
Missing RCCThe customer provided an account number but no codes.
Invalid RCCThe code entered is not registered with the agency for this reporting period.
Missing / Incorrect RatesA "Needs Attention" warning appears because a code exists but has no associated rate.
Getting Ready for a Risk Class Code (RCC) Correction

🔍 Step 1: Identify which RCC is blocking payroll

  • From the company's Panda page, click on View Washington State Info.
  • Find the RCC that is labeled "Will soft suspend in __ days" or "Deactivate & remove suspension."

👁️ Step 2: Review affected employees & wages

  • Navigate to the company's Tax Summary in Pufferfish.
  • Enter the Quarter, then type "WA Workers' Comp Insurance" (case-sensitive) and select WA under state.
  • Under actions, select Employee tax summary.
  • Switch to "Per tax view", then click Show next to the RCC that was incorrectly entered.
Processing a Wage Correction
⚠️
Before running the correction: make sure the employee has the correct risk class code listed in their employee profile and that the accurate effective date for the new RCC is in place in the state field in Panda.
  • 1
    Navigate to Employee Payrolls from the company's Panda page.
  • 2
    Under actions, click Run Auto Wage Correction Payroll.
  • 3
    Select the Beginning and End dates:
    • For current quarters: choose the most recent check date in the quarter.
    • Reminder: If the company has a monthly filing frequency, corrections should use the last day of the month as the end check date (instead of the last day of the quarter). Refer to the Monthly Filers resource document.
  • 4
    Click Preview Wage Correction to see the employee's original wages and taxes alongside the corrected wages and taxes.
  • 5
    Review the correction and if everything looks good, click Run Wage Correction to process.
Reading the Wage Correction Payroll
The company's bank account will be debited the next day to pay for all underpaid employee/employer taxes — this will be the difference between any RCC rates.

✅ Positive Check Amount

The employee is owed this amount. The employer needs to set up a reimbursement or pay the employee via check.

❌ Negative Check Amount

The employee owes this back to the company. The employer needs to set up a one-time or recurring deduction.
💡
Always review the check amount carefully before finalizing to ensure the correct adjustment direction.
Tax Filing & Payment Implications
ℹ️
Past Quarter Original Filing Process Change: Beginning with Q1 2024, TaxOps will support original filings for all Pufferfish agencies triggered after the deadline, up to the last re-file attempt date (one month after the quarter close). This ensures greater consistency in supporting original returns.
Each payroll has Subject Wages, Gross Subject Wages, and Gross Wages. Understanding the tax summary is key:
TermWhat it Means
Tax AmountTotal money paid to the tax agency.
Gross WagesTotal wages earned by the employee (often matches what we see on a paystub/salary).
Subject WagesWages subject to a specific tax. YTD subject wages should never exceed the wage base limit (e.g., California SUI has a wage base of $7,000).
Gross Subject WagesTotal wages earned that are taxable for this tax — will not reflect wage base limits, but will reflect benefits and imputed income.
What Happens Next? (Underpaid vs. Overpaid)

📉 Underpaid Tax Amounts

Debits will always happen the day after you run the AWC. Check the payroll debit date to confirm.

📈 Overpaid Tax Amounts

Verify all payments by checking if they've been made in the 20[xx] Debits/Agent Payment Summary.
Quarter StatusTaxes NOT Yet PaidTaxes Already Paid
Current Quarter Set taxes to pending in Panda. Refunds take 3–5 business days before the customer sees them. We will request the amounts in the original return at the end of the quarter.
Closed Quarters If Gusto still has the funds, file a Payments JIRA (manual NACHA) if auto wage corrections and/or tax reconciliations did not automatically trigger a refund. Customers must wait for the amended return process. Agencies send a refund check or overpayment notice directly to the company (even for state withholdings). The company pays back employees for any taxes the employee overpaid.
Tip: Recommend the employer wait until funds are returned before paying employees — but it is ultimately up to the employer.
Amendments take approximately 12–16 weeks (MasterTax) or 6 weeks (Pufferfish).

Case Reason 8 of 12
FEIN Change
Handling Federal Employer Identification Number changes — from initial outreach through full migration, including employees, contractors, payroll, and benefits.
What is an FEIN?
A Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN) is a nine-digit unique identifier issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). It serves as a tax ID for businesses, non-profit organizations, estates, trusts, and other entities operating in the United States. All companies that have hired an employee should apply for an FEIN with the IRS — this includes people who hire themselves and pay themselves wages.

🏢 Businesses

Sole proprietors, partnerships, corporations, and Limited Liability Companies (LLCs) with multiple members.

🤝 Non-profit Organizations

Charities, foundations, religious institutions, social clubs, and associations.

📋 Estates & Trusts

Estates established after an individual's death and various types of trusts.

👥 Employers

Any entity hiring employees, including businesses and nonprofits.
First Steps: FEIN Change Decision Flowchart
When an admin reaches out, use this decision tree to route the case correctly before taking any action.
ScenarioAction
Admin provides a new FEIN + has active Gusto-Managed Benefits (GMB)Route case to FEIN – Benefits queue. Do not proceed without Benefits team involvement.
Admin provides a new FEIN + no active GMB + needs a new Gusto accountProceed with the full FEIN Change process and provide next steps.
Admin provides a new FEIN + no active GMB + no new Gusto account neededApprove the FEIN in Panda and provide next steps.
Admin does NOT provide a new FEIN + confirms no new FEIN neededInstruct the admin to change their entity type in-app.
Admin does NOT provide a new FEIN + uncertain if new FEIN neededInstruct the admin to confirm with the IRS whether a new FEIN is required.
Ownership / Entity Type Changes
ℹ️
Admins often contact us about a business/entity type change — this does not always mean the company has been assigned a new FEIN. If a new company is acquiring a company that currently uses Gusto, IRS documentation is still required.

🏢 If the FEIN Did NOT Change

The admin can update their business/entity type directly in-app:

  1. Go to Taxes & Compliance → Tax Setup
  2. Next to "Federal Tax Setup," click Edit
  3. Under "Company Type," make the new selection
  4. Click Save

🔄 Business / Company Merge

When a new admin reaches out because they bought a company using Gusto and needs data migrated to the new account — we can assist, but:

  • IRS documentation is required showing the new FEIN (CP-575 or 147-C Federal EIN Verification letter)
  • CC the Primary Admin of the old company to confirm the merge is actually taking place
Self-Service FEIN Change Alert Tool
This tool enables customers to self-serve EIN updates. When an automated email notifies us of a change, follow these steps:
  • 1
    In Salesforce, click the Inapp EIN request number to open the Panda request.
  • 2
    In Panda, review the change.
  • 3
    Under "EIN change," click the Company Name to review the company's details.
  • 4
    Under "Submission," review the details the employer wants changed (new EIN, company name, entity type, etc.).
    EIN Verification – Pass: System confirmed the new EIN is valid. Still confirm it is not a duplicate (search EIN in Panda). If a duplicate exists, check account creation date, who made it, and its status. If all looks good, approve the SF case, send a basic macro, log in to the dormant account, continue setup, and ask if a migration is needed (standard FEIN process).
    EIN Verification – Fail: EIN did not pass the TIN check. Create an SFDC case and ask for documentation (IRS CP-575 or LTR-147). Send the standard FEIN macro to create a new account.
  • 5
    Either Approve or Reject the change and leave a comment.
💡
If the admin does not have IRS documentation, they can contact the IRS at 1 (800) 829-4933 to request a Form 147C. It can be faxed directly to them.
Do We Need a New Gusto Account?
New FEINs typically require creating a new Gusto account — but not always.

🆕 New Account NOT Needed

If the admin wants to update/correct their FEIN and Gusto has not yet filed with the IRS — we can edit the FEIN directly in Panda:

  • Go to the company Panda page → click Edit Company in the top right corner
  • Alert the admin about any tax payments already made to the IRS — they will need to move those payments to the correct FEIN with the IRS directly
  • IRS proof is required (CP-575 or Letter 147C) — state agency documentation alone is not sufficient

🆕 New Account IS Required

  • If Gusto has already filed with the IRS, we cannot edit the FEIN — the admin must create a new Gusto account with the new FEIN
  • A change in business name alone typically does not require a new FEIN (see Change a Company's Legal or Trade Name IKB)
GMB Check — Does the Company Have Active Benefits?
🚫
Before reaching out to the admin: check if the company has active Gusto-Managed Benefits (GMB). If yes, route the case to the Tier 2 FEIN – Benefits queue.

Step 1: Check for Benefits pill

In Panda, go to the company's main page and check for the Benefits pill at the top of the screen. If the pill is there, confirm the benefits are active (expired benefits = not a FEIN-Benefits case).

Step 2: Confirm GMB via Hippo

Click Hippo in the top right corner of Panda. (If there is no Hippo button, the company does not have GMB.) Scroll to Current Benefits → Active Subscriptions to confirm.
ℹ️
To reroute to FEIN – Benefits: From the case, click Re-route Case → Do you want to route to Engagement? Yes → Are you routing to a specialization team? Yes → Specialization: FEIN – Benefits → Click Next.
Setting Proper Expectations
FEIN Changes require a lot of collaboration and communication. Set clear expectations with the admin upfront.

📋 What We CAN Migrate

  • Employee name, date of birth, SSN, home/work addresses
  • Withholding elections
  • Direct deposit information
  • Active contractors
  • Guideline 401(k) (before payroll migration)
  • NEXT Insurance (9-step process)
  • Contractor payments (full or partial year)

🚫 What CANNOT Be Migrated

  • Employees' emergency contact information
  • Recovery emails and phone numbers
  • PTO/sick policies and balances
  • Paid Holiday policies
  • Externally managed benefits information
  • Company organizational charts
  • Employee & company custom documents
  • Payroll Schedules
  • Time Tracking and Hours
  • Administrator permissions
  • Tax exemptions for the company or employees
  • Terminated employee records
  • Previous year W-2 history, historical tax filings/payments
⚠️
Payroll Migration Expectations: If the FEIN change impacts a previous year, the customer is responsible for correcting and amending prior-year filings — Gusto handles corrections for the current year only. The admin must confirm the effective date of the FEIN change (which payrolls stay under the old FEIN vs. move to the new one). They should contact a tax professional or the IRS if unsure. The admin must also decide how to handle any current-quarter taxes already remitted to the agency.
4-Phase Migration Timeline
  • 1
    Initial Outreach / Confirm Details — Verify FEIN, determine if new Gusto account is needed, check for GMB, set proper expectations with the admin using the FEIN Changes IKB and Tier 2 FEIN Macros.
  • 2
    EE/CTR Migration — Migrate employees and contractors using the BOSS tool. Transfer NEXT Insurance (9 steps). Transfer Guideline 401(k) — this must happen before payroll migration.
  • 3
    Payroll Migration — Use the Payroll Migration Tool. All steps must happen on the same day. Determine contractor payment migration scope (full year vs. partial year). Reverse applicable payrolls on old account after migration.
  • 4
    Recap / Action Items — Confirm FEIN Change in Panda (turns off filing fees on old account). Admin cancels old Gusto account. Recap what was migrated, list remaining action items, and set expectations about payment/filing activation.
Phase 2: Migrating Employees & Contractors (BOSS Tool)
The BOSS tool in Panda is used to copy employee (EE) and contractor (CTR) profiles from one company to another. This transfers PII/PHI — handle with care.
  • 1
    In Panda, go to Customers → Migrate EE/CTR Profiles.
  • 2
    Find the company IDs for both the original and new company in Panda.
  • 3
    Enter the original (old) and new company IDs into the appropriate fields. Confirm the company names match, then click Copy Humans.
  • 4
    Verify EE/CTR data is listed. Pro Tip: Refresh the page a couple of times — the tool doesn't always pick up every EE/CTR on first load.
  • 5
    All people are in "Draft" state at this point. If you need to delete any, click the row number and press Backspace. Undo accidental deletions with Command + Z.
  • 6
    Click Review and correct any errors (rows in red). Click on a highlighted row to see the specific error.
  • 7
    Once reviewed and corrected, submit. The tool will allow submission as long as at least one valid row exists — only rows without errors will be migrated.
  • 8
    Repeat steps 4–7 to migrate domestic contractors (or employees if you started with contractors). Note: International Contractors cannot be migrated with this tool — they must be added manually by the customer.

Visual walkthrough: Migrating Employees & Contractors (BOSS Tool)

Transfer NEXT Insurance (Workers' Comp)
⚠️
If the customer has an active Workers' Comp policy through NEXT, you must transfer it to the new account — it is not automatically transferred.

Steps for Gusto

  1. In Panda, go to "Company Info" and check for a Workers' Comp policy. If the status shows anything other than "External Policy" or "No Policy," the customer has a NEXT policy.
  2. When there's an FEIN change on an existing account, we send an update to NEXT via the "Daily Business Changes" report (we do not include actual FEIN since it's PII).
  3. Loop in NEXT by CC'ing gustosupport@apintego.com on an email from the case. The admin must provide: effective date of FEIN change, company name changes, new FEIN, ownership, each owner's name and ownership percentage, address changes, changes to company operations, reason for suspending existing Gusto account.

NEXT Transfer Process (9 Steps)

  1. NEXT provides the customer a form to update the existing policy.
  2. Customer signs and returns the form to NEXT.
  3. NEXT forwards documentation to the insurance carrier for review.
  4. Carrier reviews — usually takes 5–7 business days.
  5. NEXT receives updated policy info and changes the company's FEIN in their system.
  6. Policy info is sent to Gusto via recurring sync; customer is prompted to "connect" the policy.
  7. Customer receives an email from Gusto with a "To-Do" notification on their homepage.
  8. Once connected, the sync between the new Gusto account and NEXT is live.
  9. ACH info on the new account is uploaded to NEXT once enrollment is received. Policy info on the old account is cleared when NEXT sends an "inactive" enrollment.
🚫
Customer expectations: If payrolls are run on the new FEIN before the NEXT policy is connected, premiums or coverage may be missed and a retroactive debit may occur. NEXT resolves lapses within 30–45 days, or payments may be deemed late. If the customer doesn't connect the policy in a timely manner, it risks cancellation — we cannot send payroll or upload banking info until the customer consents.
Transfer Guideline 401(k) — BEFORE Payroll Migration
🚫
This step MUST be completed before the payroll migration. The 401(k) does not automatically transfer to the new account. If done out of order, it creates significant downstream issues that cannot be reversed.
Advise the plan sponsor to make changes from their Guideline Administrator account:
  • 1
    Sign in to the administrator dashboard.
  • 2
    Navigate to Settings by clicking the dropdown in the upper right corner.
  • 3
    Select Edit Company Information and update the necessary fields.
  • 4
    Upload supporting documentation (e.g., Secretary of State filing) to the Resource Library of their dashboard.
  • 5
    Notify Guideline by emailing clients@guideline.com.
  • 6
    The admin can run payroll again once Guideline confirms the FEIN change is complete and their 401(k) account is connected to the new Gusto account. Note: Annual maximum contributions do not need to be updated per employee on the new account in Panda — existing contributions are included during the payroll migration step.
Phase 3: Payroll Migration
⚠️
Prerequisites before starting: Admin has finished onboarding (bank verified, state tax details entered); all benefits set up with same benefit name; all employees migrated; NEXT/Guideline looped in if necessary; effective date confirmed; admin confirmed which taxes need to be debited.
🚫
All steps below must happen on the same day.
  • 1
    Go to the original company's Panda page.
  • 2
    From the Actions dropdown, select FEIN Change – Migrate Payrolls.
  • 3
    Enter the new company's ID and the effective date of the new FEIN.
  • 4
    Click Link Companies.
  • 5
    You will see payrolls with a check date after the effective date — these must be migrated in order.
  • 6
    Click Migrate Payroll to produce the unprocessed external payroll under the new account.
  • 7
    Click Debit Taxes & Finish and select which taxes to debit, or mark as prepaid (if you do not want to debit them).
  • 8
    After verifying, click Finish & Process.
  • 9
    You'll be directed back to the payroll migration page to continue processing any other payrolls. Note: The tool remembers your tax selections from the most recent payroll migrated.
  • 10
    Repeat steps 6–8 until all payroll data is migrated to the new account, then exit the tool.
  • 11
    Go to the new company account to verify all intended payrolls have been transferred. If any are missing, manually add as an external payroll.
  • 12
    Once payrolls have been migrated, reverse them under the old account and amend any impacted filings.

Visual walkthrough: Payroll Migration

Contractor Payment Migration
The steps depend on whether contractor payments need to be migrated for the full year or only part of the year.

Full Year Migration

  1. From the old account, download the Contractor Payment report to get the year-to-date (YTD) payment totals.
  2. From the new account, go to Contractor Payments in-app and process historical contractor payments with the YTD totals.
  3. From the old account, reverse the contractor payments and disable 1099 filings for all applicable contractors — since all payments for the year should now be reported under the new account.

Partial Year Migration

  1. From the old account, download the Contractor Payment report and filter for a custom date range from the effective date.
  2. Note the date-range totals from the report.
  3. From the old account, correct contractor payments by reversing all applicable payments from after the effective date.
  4. From the new account, go to Contractor Payments in-app and process historical contractor payments for the applicable period.

Visual walkthrough: Migrating Payrolls

Post-Migration: Payroll Reversals on the Old Account
After migrating all payrolls, go to the old company account and complete the following:
  • 1
    Reverse the applicable payrolls under the old account. Check for any failed filings in the Payroll Reversals (Entire) tab in Panda.
  • 2
    Process tax recons (if some wages remain on the account).
  • 3
    Review the tax summary — it should say $0.00 for the expected quarters.
  • 4
    Mark affected company filings for amendment, including year-end forms (generate W-2c forms if applicable).
  • 5
    Stop any state filings when account numbers have not changed — create a TaxOps Jira requesting the applicable state filings be stopped and assign to a captain.
  • 6
    If payrolls were already run on the new FEIN account for a current or past quarter that Gusto filed for, go to the new FEIN account → run tax recons for impacted quarters → mark quarters and annual forms for amendment when needed.
Mass Payroll Reversal Tool
The Mass Payroll Reversal tool allows you to reverse multiple payrolls at once — use this for FEIN changes instead of the standard reversal flow.
  • 1
    From the old company Panda, click Employee Payrolls under "Payments."
  • 2
    Under the "Actions" section, click Run Mass Payroll Reversals for FEIN Changes. The company ID should be prefilled. Enter the effective date in the "Start Date" field, your Salesforce Case Number, and a comment indicating these reversals are due to an FEIN change.
  • 3
    Click Preview Reversals — you will be asked to confirm the check dates and payrolls being reversed.
  • 4
    Once you have processed the mass reversal, approve the reversals individually. Start from the most recent and work your way to the oldest. Tax reconciliation payrolls should be reversed before any other payrolls in that quarter to avoid failed reversals.
Phase 4: Cancel Account & Turn Off Filing Fees
Once the FEIN migration is complete, the admin is responsible for canceling their old Gusto account. Before canceling, the filing fees must be turned off by confirming the FEIN change in Panda.
  • 1
    In the old company's Panda page, go to Actions → Confirm FEIN Change. Once clicked, you can confirm it went through by trying to repeat the step — the "Confirm FEIN Change" option should no longer be visible.
  • 2
    Once the Gustie has confirmed the FEIN Change in the old account, the company can cancel their account through the account cancellation flow.

To wrap up the FEIN change case, follow up and set expectations with the admin:

Explain what was migrated and how the admin can see this information in their new account.

⚡ Account Activation

The new account is not activated for payments and filings until the admin processes their first payroll (if they haven't already done so).

⚠️ Late Filing Disclaimer

Late payment and/or filing can cause a notice with penalties/interest.

✅ Admin Action Items

Cancel old Gusto account (turn off filing fees in Panda first); correct and file any forms outside of Gusto; contact IRS and/or state agencies to transfer taxes from old to new account.

Case Reason 9 of 12
Local Taxes
Understanding local tax basics, common tax types by state, address verification, and working with Symmetry to resolve geocode issues.
Section 1: The Basics
Local taxes are imposed by cities and counties. The tax jurisdiction typically aligns with the boundaries of the municipality or county. In certain instances, the tax jurisdiction may be a school district or a district established solely for tax purposes.

🔍 What are local taxes?

  • Imposed by cities and counties
  • Tax jurisdiction aligns with the municipality or county boundaries
  • Can also be a school district or district established solely for tax purposes

💼 Who is responsible?

  • Typically, companies are only required to withhold taxes for counties based on the work location
  • If an employer opts to withhold taxes based on the employee's home address, they must elect for courtesy withholding

📋 What info determines local taxes?

  • Local taxes are withheld based on the employee's work address and home address
Section 2: How Does Gusto Determine Which Local Taxes to Withhold?

📍 Address Analysis

The Address Analysis tool in Panda is used to analyze and verify the addresses of employees and companies. It helps identify discrepancies or errors in address data, allowing corrections to avoid payroll and tax submission issues.

🔬 What is Symmetry (STE)?

STE (Symmetry Tax Engine) is a product used by Gusto to stay updated on tax rates that apply universally to all or most employers. This allows Gusto to automatically update certain tax rates, limits, and calculations without requiring customers to manually update them.

What if a customer disagrees with Gusto's address verification?
  1. Engagement reviews address analysis against state site calculations — if Gusto does not match, submit a ticket to Symmetry.
  2. Symmetry reviews and either confirms the current results or updates their system to new settings.
  3. Based on ticket response, Gustie either explains current results to admin or performs a geocode override after Symmetry approval.
Section 3: Common Local Taxes by State

🏛️ Ohio Local Taxes

  • Municipal tax: Employers are required to withhold municipal taxes for the area where the employee works. Can be collected by the city, a neighboring city, or outsourced to a third-party collector.
  • School district tax: Imposed on residents who live within a specific school district. Employers are responsible for withholding school district income tax from employees who reside in a school district that has this tax.
  • JEDD/JEDZ: Applied to residents of a specified area to fund economic development projects.

📎 For more info, refer to the Ohio Local Taxes IKB.

🏛️ Pennsylvania Local Taxes

  • Earned Income Tax (EIT): Withholding rate is determined by comparing the employee's home location EIT rate and the work location's Non-Resident EIT Rate. The higher of the two rates is the applicable rate.
  • Local Service Tax (LST): Payable by all individuals who hold a job or profession within a taxing jurisdiction imposing the tax.
  • School District Taxes: School Districts in PA can enact an earned income tax on residents of up to 1% and are not permitted to tax nonresidents.
  • PSD Codes: Six-digit numbers that identify each municipality in Pennsylvania.
  • Scranton Payroll Preparation Tax (HAB-PPT): All individuals or businesses operating within Scranton must register and pay this tax if they have not done so previously.

📎 For more info, refer to the Pennsylvania Local Taxes IKB.

Section 4: Courtesy Withholding
Admins can elect to withhold income taxes in the employee's resident state.

What is courtesy withholding? Courtesy withholding occurs when an employer voluntarily registers for a withholding account in a state where they don't have a business location. This is done as a courtesy to withhold income tax for an employee's home state through payroll.

In-app: When the admin elects courtesy withholding, a pop-up will inform the admin that they must register with the corresponding state agencies.

  • A non-residency certificate may be required when setting up courtesy withholding, and Gusto does not provide this document. The document is to be kept on file for internal company purposes.
⚠️ If necessary, be sure to process a Tax Recon after electing courtesy withholding!

In-app: Electing Courtesy Withholding

When adding an employee, the admin is prompted:
"Pay home taxes?"

  • Yes — Gusto should withhold and pay the employee's home taxes
  • No — Employee will be responsible for paying home taxes

In Panda: Electing Courtesy Withholding

Navigate to the employee's Home Addresses section in Panda. Check the "Pay Home Taxes (Courtesy)" checkbox.

  • Effective date will be shown alongside the address entry
  • Process a Tax Recon as needed after changes
Section 5: Address Verification — Using Address Analysis in Panda
When an administrator questions why a tax is being withheld or why they are being asked to register for a specific local tax when they believe they should not be liable, we need the affected employee's name and address.

Pull the employee's profile up in Panda and select Address Analysis to see the current tax results. This page breaks the employee's address down to the county, latitude, and longitude coordinates — allowing for a more granular understanding of the exact location from which the tax is derived.

📊 Example 1: Comparing PA's Address Lookup Tool to Panda

When a customer disputes a local tax result, compare the state's address lookup tool to Gusto's Address Analysis:

  • Run the employee's address through the state's lookup tool (e.g., PA's address lookup)
  • Check the resulting PSD Code, EIT rate, and LST amount
  • Compare against what Panda's Address Analysis shows for the same address
  • If there is a discrepancy — for example, Gusto shows "Washington EIT" but the state site shows "Northern Lehigh SD" — this is the basis for a Symmetry ticket
⚠️ Note: Gusto shows the employee is taxed to Washington, but the ER states it should be taxed to Northern Lehigh. This discrepancy triggers a Symmetry ticket.
Section 6: Working with Symmetry

📝 How to Submit a Ticket to Symmetry

Sign into Symmetry through Okta and click "Need Help? Submit a Ticket".

Fill out the highlighted fields as follows:

  • Symmetry product: Symmetry Select
  • Select Product: Symmetry Tax Engine (STE)
  • STE Country: U.S.
  • Reason for Inquiry: Calculation Results
  • Subject: SFDC #
  • Description: Include the following:
    • Impacted Address (home and/or work address)
    • Current tax results
    • Expected/desired tax results
    • Confirmations from agency (screenshot of address in Munstats and results)
    • Anything else used to determine taxability

✅ Next Steps: Symmetry AGREES

Once Symmetry updates their database, refresh the data in Panda using the Geocode Overrides tool.

  1. Navigate to Payroll Compliance in Panda
  2. Click on Geocode Overrides
  3. Click 'New override'
  4. Enter the impacted address and click 'Create'
  5. Enter the same address in the search bar and select it (fields will auto-populate to most recent STE info)
  6. Click copy all
  7. Enter the reason for the update
  8. Use SFDC and STE case number
  9. Click submit
  10. Click re-geocode all (required for override to be performed)
  11. Double check override was successful in the address analysis section
  12. Check address analysis for correct PSD and locality; make corrections as needed
  13. Confirm with admin when this should be effective and make corrections. Tax Recon should recognize the changes.

❌ Next Steps: Symmetry DOES NOT AGREE

Notify the administrator that our Geo-Locator has confirmed the taxation. If they decide to override it, they will be entirely responsible for any issues related to the change.
  1. On the main Panda page, go to Payroll Compliance Header > Geocode Overrides
  2. Click "New Override" and enter the address to correct (omit 'Street Address 2' / apartment number)
  3. Click "Create"
  4. Enter each different address separately as its own individual override (cannot override multiple addresses in one instance)
    • Note: System is sensitive — "dr" vs "drive" are counted as two separate addresses
  5. Find another address that will pull the admin's desired taxation
    • Tip: Use Google Maps to review the locality border and locate an address close to the current one but within the correct boundary
⚠️ This process will temporarily override the address(es) in Panda so payrolls will be correct going forward. If the address is modified or a new employee utilizes the same address, the incorrect taxes will be pulled.

📋 Next Steps: Symmetry Asks for STE Logs

What is a STE Log?

  • A detailed code/engineering-heavy file that details the resulting payroll calculation
  • Shows settings for all payroll data elements, address info, taxable wages, benefits, and more
  • Pulled from Buildkite (Okta permissions required) and shared with STE support

How to Get a STE Log

  • Post in #symmetry-ste-logs-using-buildkite via Slack
  • Provide the Payroll Item Run UUID for the team
  • Finding the UUID: Find the payroll in question → Find the individual → Click "view" → The Payroll Item page has a section called "Input Payroll Data" — UUID lives there (at the bottom of the page)
  • Reference Confluence instructions steps 4b–4vi for visual guidance
Section 7: Troubleshooting Tips

🔧 Error Adding a Geo-Override?

You can delete the override and try again:

  1. Start on the Geocode Overrides page
  2. Find the address you were overriding
  3. Click View for that address
  4. Click Delete

✅ Ensure All Codes Are Populating Correctly

If any codes are missing and should be there, it may block payroll.

Example (Colorado):

  • State Code: 08 (Colorado)
  • County Code: 031 (Jefferson County)
  • City Code: 201738 (Lakewood)

🌍 Check the "Geocode State" Under Usages

  • Successful: geocode_success
  • Unsuccessful: geocode_error
  • Click "re-geocode all" to try and refresh data to be successful

Case Reason 10 of 12
Sales Tax Exempt
Processing sales tax exemptions using Gusto's third-party partner Avalara and the CertCapture portal.
Legal Background: South Dakota v. Wayfair (2018)
Online, subscription-based services are now required to charge sales tax in specific jurisdictions. In June 2018 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that states can collect sales tax on online sales even if a business has no physical presence there. This shifted collection from the seller's physical location to where the product is sold — affecting 22+ states and local jurisdictions.

📍 Before Wayfair

Sales tax was only required if the seller had a physical presence (nexus) in the state. Online stores had an unfair advantage over brick-and-mortar stores.

⚖️ After Wayfair

States can now require any online seller — including SaaS companies like Gusto — to collect and remit sales tax based on where customers are located.
What is Gusto Sales Tax?
💡
TL;DR — Legislation deems software subscription services like Gusto taxable. Gusto is legally required to collect and remit sales tax in affected jurisdictions unless an exemption is in place.

1 · Why does Gusto collect sales tax?

Gusto is legally required to collect and remit sales tax in affected jurisdictions unless an exemption is in place. This affects over 22 states and local jurisdictions.

2 · How is sales tax determined?

The rate is assessed based on a company's filing address. It can range from 8.5–10% and you can find the company's sales tax charge in Panda and on invoices.

3 · Why might a company be exempt?

Common exemptions include non-profits, religious or edu orgs, and resellers/accountants who manage multiple accounts. Local legislation can also determine exemptions. We cannot advise on if a company is exempt or not.
Key Rules

🚫 No Refunds

Gusto cannot compliantly refund sales tax. It is the customer's responsibility to ensure their exemption is set up in the correct time frame. Like returning an item to a store — you don't get back the sales tax you already paid.

🔗 Avalara Handles Validation

Gusto's third-party partner Avalara (via CertCapture) processes and validates all exemption documents. Avalara takes 3 business days to validate. If a document is rejected, Avalara emails the customer directly.

👤 Customer Uploads Their Own Docs

Never upload documentation for the customer. The customer must go through the CertCapture portal and upload their own documents themselves.
Avalara & the CertCapture Portal
Most of the exemption flow takes place within Avalara's CertCapture portal — not directly in Gusto.

🏢 Who is Avalara?

  • Our third-party sales-tax partner that processes and validates exemption documentation through the CertCapture portal
  • The Gusto/Avalara partnership allows Avalara to validate documents and sync the exemption over to Gusto accounts

⚙️ How It Works

  • Avalara creates a unique link for each company to upload their exemption documentation
  • Gusties can send the link through Panda or via the CertCapture portal
  • The customer uploads their documentation to their unique link
  • Avalara takes 3 business days to validate/invalidate documents
  • Avalara will only email the customer if a document was rejected
What to Find in Panda

Go to the company's billing/payment plan details page → Tax Exemption Information. From here you can view the upcoming invoice sales tax amount under Payment Plan Details → Calculate Sales Tax.

  • Customer Code — Used by Avalara to identify this company. Needed when calling Avalara. Search by this in Avalara's customer page.
  • Certificates section — Shows all attempts, their status (pending / valid / invalid), signed date, expiration date, and jurisdiction.
  • Tax Exemption Request Form Link — The unique CertCapture link for this company. Send this to the customer so they can upload their exemption documentation.
  • "Generate new link" button — Use this to create or regenerate a unique CertCapture link for the company.

Payment Plan Details — Calculate Sales Tax link

Customer Workflow — CertCapture (7 Steps)
🔔
Reminder: We should not be uploading documentation for the customer. The customer must go through this flow and upload the documents themselves via the CertCapture portal.
  • 1
    Customer opens the unique CertCapture link sent via email
  • 2
    Clicks Add exemption certificate to begin
  • 3
    Selects the exposure zone (state of filing address)
  • 4
    Selects the exemption reason (e.g., Charitable/Exempt Org)
  • 5
    Imports the exemption certificate and completes all required information fields
  • 6
    Electronically signs and authorizes the submission
  • 7
    Submits — Avalara validates within 3 business days. Once validated, the exemption syncs to the Gusto account.

Calling Avalara
📞
Dedicated Gusto line: 206-826-2252. Our friends at Avalara are super helpful! You can speak with the rep yourself or warm-transfer the customer.
  • Have both portals pulled up before calling: Panda (Tax Exemption Information page) and Avalara's customer page (search by Customer Code or company name)
  • Identify the customer using their Customer Code or company name
  • Avalara can tell you why a document was invalidated and what documentation is needed based on the customer's nexus (location) and exemption reason
  • Like Gusto, Avalara cannot technically advise on whether a company qualifies for an exemption — but they can guide on the correct documentation
  • Take notes on verbiage, relay customer questions and concerns, and ask technical questions on the customer's behalf
  • Please Note: If you encounter any issues that require Avalara system access, reach out to your PE — they can provide necessary insights and/or assistance

Manual Wage Correction (MWC)
A last-resort tool that directly adjusts wages, taxes, and benefit amounts in historical payrolls — use only when no other tool can fix the issue.
Section 1: The Basics of MWCs
What is the Manual Wage Correction tool? A tool that allows us to directly change an employee's wages, taxes, and benefit amounts. This tool is very flexible and should only be used in the following scenarios:
  • Accommodating for other tools (AWC, benefit adjustment, recons, etc.) not working properly/as expected
  • Workaround to include custom post-tax deductions on historicals/externals
  • One-off tax situations that other tools cannot accommodate (e.g., unique minister housing requirement that falls outside of normal tax behavior)
📢
THE GOLDEN RULE: If a different action can be taken, DO NOT use the Manual Wage Correction tool.
Ex. reversal, recon, benefit adjustment, external, auto wage correction

THE MANUAL WAGE CORRECTION TOOL IS A LAST RESORT!
⚠️
DISCLAIMER: Triple check your work. Because these adjustments are manual, they can be error-prone — there are no guardrails in the tool to catch mistakes when calculating taxes/SW.

It's important to remember not to drive wages into the negative. TRIPLE CHECK YOUR WORK when creating or approving them.
Benefit Adjuster Tool vs. MWC Tool

What is the difference and why would we use one vs. the other?

Benefit Adjuster

  • Used to adjust benefit amounts on past payrolls
  • Automatically calculates changes to SW and tax amounts
  • Can adjust multiple EEs at once
  • Creates a wage correction payroll/pay-stub for each check date
  • Requires approval by another advocate

MWC

  • Requires advocate to manually calculate GSW, SW and sometimes Gross wages taxes
  • Can only adjust 1 EE at a time
  • Will primarily be used for one-off adjustments
  • Creates a wage correction payroll/pay-stub for each check date
  • Requires approval by another advocate or PE
AWC Tool vs. MWC Tool

What is the difference and why would we use one vs. the other?

AWC

  • Automatically calculates taxes and subject wages
  • Used in 3 specific situations (exemptions, backdated address changes, and incorrect risk class codes)
  • Does not need another advocate's approval
  • Can adjust multiple employees at once

MWC

  • Requires advocate to manually calculate GSW, SW, sometimes Gross wages and taxes
  • Needs to be approved by another advocate or PE
  • Can only adjust one employee at a time
Section 2: Prepping for and Running a MWC

⚠️ Most MWCs Need PE Approval

There is one MWC reason that does not require a PE to approve:

  • Minister Housing

Outside of this reason, it is required for a PE to review and reference the checklist and also provide feedback via a TPO or Feature Request Jira to the product team to make sure we limit the amount of manual processing outside of the approved workarounds.

🔍 How to Prepare for a MWC

  1. Determine what the issue/bug is and how it is impacting the tax summary
  2. Confirm that no other tools can be used to fix the issue. Create a TPO or Feature Request Jira if needed.
  3. Get PE Approval
  4. Anticipate tax summary changes by calculating the changes to the benefits, taxes, subject wages, and gross subject wages
  5. Double check your calculations
  6. Check for potential debits or refunds:
    • Debits: Double check company join date and tax filing status for affected quarters to determine what Gusto can/can't debit for — we can only debit for a tax if we filed successful original returns in the respective quarter
    • Refunds: Gusto can only refund the company for a tax if we have not yet remitted it to the agency — if a tax has been remitted, the company will be refunded by the agency once amended filings are filed & processed
  7. Set clear expectations with the admin about any refunds, debits, amendments, etc.
    • Confirm any debits with the admin & warn them of P&I
    • If we aren't able to debit/amend, the company will need to handle the filing and any associated payment outside of Gusto
Running the MWC — Step by Step

Steps 1 & 2 — Open the MWC Tool

Step 1

In the EE Panda profile, click on Create Wage Correction Payroll (found under Sensitive Actions in the left sidebar).

Step 2

Click on Manual Wage Correction at the top of the screen (as opposed to Auto Wage Correction).

Step 3 — Enter Check Date, Pay Period & Comment

  • Adjusting 1 specific payroll: Check date and pay period must match that payroll
  • Adjusting an entire closed quarter: Check date = last day of the quarter; pay period covers the entire quarter
  • Adjusting an open quarter (QTD): Check date = most recent payroll's check date; pay period = start of quarter through end of most recent pay period
    • We cannot set the check date in the future — if there is a processed payroll with a future check date, reverse & rerun it, or wait until after that check date
  • Monthly filing frequency: Process corrections using the check dates for the last of the month(s), not at the end of the quarter. Pay period start and end should match the 1st and last day of the month.

Explanation example: "12345678 adjusting simple IRA ER contributions (bene adjuster tool is not working properly)"

Step 4 — Adjust Tax & Benefit Amounts

  • Adjust the Tax Amount, Subject Wages, and Gross Subject Wages as needed
  • Do not adjust Gross Wages unless it is for minister housing
  • Adjust benefit amounts if needed
  • For tax amounts, SW, GSW, GW and benefits: enter a positive or negative amount to increase or decrease the amounts compared to what's currently being reported (unlike a Benefit Adjustment — you are not entering the total correct amount)
🚫 The Gross Wage box SHOULD only be edited for minister housing. Do not touch this section otherwise.

Step 6

Double check your calculations, then click Create Payroll Item at the bottom of the screen.

Step 7

Send the Panda link to your PE for approval (or peer if it is for minister housing or simple IRAs).

Section 3: After Running a MWC

💰 Confirm "Payroll Taxes Status" — Will the company be debited or get refunds?

1) Check "Liability Status"

  • Pending:
    • Negative amount → Gusto will refund the company directly
    • Positive amount → Gusto will debit the company
  • Prepaid — company needs to handle taxes outside of Gusto:
    • Positive amount → Company must pay the agency directly
    • Negative amount → Agency will refund the company once filings/amendments are processed

2) For tax refunds — verify Gusto has actually paid

If "Liability Status" shows as prepaid, confirm that Gusto has actually paid this tax. Sometimes Panda is incorrect!

  1. Go to the company's main Panda page
  2. Click on "Agent Payments" under Taxes
  3. Filter by "Agent State" on the left-hand side
  4. Find the applicable agency & quarter
  5. If the Draft column shows "yes" → tax needs to be refunded by Gusto (not yet paid) → click "Set as Pending" under Payroll Taxes Status
  6. If the Draft column shows "no" → tax has already been remitted and will be refunded by the agency

🔄 Don't Forget to Run Recons

Why Recons are important: Reconciliations ensure that taxes stay as up-to-date as possible. Running a tax recon after key events — such as employee relocations or SUI rate updates — ensures the company avoids notices and remains compliant. Downstream errors and additional Gustie work can also be avoided when recons are run promptly.

Worth Noting:

  • The objective is to not have any auto reconciliation payroll results generate. This step is basically a safety net to ensure the MWC is fully accurate and no other wages are changing as a result
  • If a change is generated on the draft, investigate and determine the root cause of the issue, resolve it, run the draft auto reconciliation payroll again until nothing is created, then run the real auto reconciliation payroll
  • Make sure to run a draft recon for the quarter you adjusted and any subsequent quarters in that calendar year to catch any potential downstream changes
  • Some scenarios may occur where you are instructed NOT to run a reconciliation — this is rare but can occur when the recon is attempting to override the changes from the MWC

📄 Amendments

Changes to wages and taxes for previous quarters require amended filings.

  • Any changes to wages/taxes for prior quarters will require an amendment
  • Gusto can only generate an amendment if we successfully filed the original filing for them
    • Double check if we generated the filings and if they were successful within the Quarterly Form Filing section of Panda
  • Make sure to leave a detailed comment in the appropriate Quarterly Form Filings page with your case number, but keep it free of Gusto jargon
  • If you're adjusting wages for a prior calendar year, a W-2C should automatically generate
Section 4: Approval 101 — Approval Checklist
When reviewing a MWC you should check all of the following:
  • ☐ Is this for minister housing?
  • ☐ Did you walk through the MWC as if you were running it yourself?
  • ☐ Is the math correct on the MWC?
  • ☐ Does it respect wage bases appropriately?
  • ☐ If adding a benefit, has the taxability been appropriately accounted for?
    • ☐ Did they adjust the correct taxes?
  • ☐ Did the advocate adjust GSW for Additional Medicare if necessary?
  • ☐ Are we debiting for taxes?
  • ☐ Did the advocate leave a comment for context?
  • ☐ Did you check the SFDC case?
  • ☐ Is the check date correct?
  • ☐ Did they use the correct tax rates?
Section 5: MWC Demo Cases
Since MWCs are typically used for one-off situations where other tools are not working properly, for the sake of practice on these examples please assume our other tools (Benefit adjustment, AWC, etc.) are not adjusting properly.

📧 Example #1

"Hi Gusto,

My employee Kurt Vonnegut recently updated his contribution amount for medical insurance but I forgot to update it in Gusto on time. Can you help me adjust his last payroll to reflect a $150.00 employee deduction?

Thank you!"

📧 Example #2

"Hi Gusto,

My employee Harper Lee has a weird tax situation where some of her wages are actually not subject to Social Security and Medicare taxes. Can you help me update her last payroll so that only $2,500.00 is subject to Social Security and Medicare? I've already gotten documentation from Regina's CPA confirming that this is compliant for her.

Thank you!"

📧 Example #3

"Hi Gusto,

My employee Cormac McCarthy should have had a $100 post-tax deduction on his most recent payroll that was not included when processing the payroll in Gusto. I ended up doing that payroll via check instead of direct deposit, and removed the $100 from his check amount when I wrote him the check. Can you help me correct the reporting for his most recent check date to include that $100 post-tax deduction?

Thank you!"
